correctness.rationale: For every finite pointed G-set, each transitive source orbit has exactly h_ij equivariant maps to a target orbit. A transitive G-map onto a different type strictly decreases orbit size, so a cycle must stay in one isotypic component. Nilpotence is equivalent to acyclicity of those components. Each component is a rooted labeled forest with R_i external exits and w_i choices per internal edge; the reduced directed Laplacian determinant R_i(R_i+m_i w_i)^(m_i-1) yields the claimed product. For same-type and distinct-type two-orbit probes the formulas 1+2w and 1+h_ij+h_ji follow. Strict size descent or equal-size no-map condition permits orientation recovery, hence the table of marks. The standalone checker independently enumerates point maps, iterates them to zero for C2,C3,C4,S3,V4, and reconstructs the S3 mark table; it is finite corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The new factorization classifies a natural nilpotent stratum of every finite pointed G-set endomorphism monoid uniformly for any finite group, including arbitrary stabilizer mixtures. The short two-orbit probe counts recover every subgroup fixed-point mark, a standard structural invariant of finite permutation representations, rather than merely recomputing known values. The nilpotency index is also controlled by the longest weighted stabilizer quotient chain. These are motivated all-family structural and inverse statements; no unproved downstream theorem is required.
